thread:
anya: FYI bringing up aorta7b (≈7B) int4 canary. Seeing intermittent OOMs in perf tests when max_new_tokens >= 256. Memory maps show fragmentation spikes after a handful of requests. Rolling back canary until triage. :thinking_face:

mike: can you paste the root config + batch settings? are we using prefetch/kvcache?

anya: config: ```model: aorta7b
quant: int4
batch_size: 4
max_new_tokens: 512
prefetch: true
kv_trim_threshold: 0.15
allocator: default```

eva: quick note — synthetic perf runs show alloc churn at token ~180-220. Looks like the KV cache isn't compacting between sessions; fragmentation grows across short-lived requests.

sol: @anya can you attach the oom stack? infra-bot might have heap stats. :eyes: 

infra-bot: alert: container/runner-42 OOM at 2025-06-15T18:22:11Z. RSS peaked 11.8GB; GPU mem 31.2GB. thread_id=0x7f... logs: /internal/logs/runner-42/oom. (auto-report)

anya: paste from logs: ```OOM: alloc failed at new_kv_slot (size 131072)
slot_free: 12
compaction_runs: 0
prefetch_hits: 3
requests_since_warmup: 8```

mike: hypothesis: prefetch + large batch + long max_new_tokens -> transient fragmentation. Two quick mitigations: 1) set max_new_tokens default to 128 on canary; 2) set batch_size: 1 or enable soft-reserve. Also try allocator=jemalloc (to reduce fragmentation).

eva: can we test kv_trim_threshold=0.4 and compaction_period=2 (runs per 1000 requests) temporarily? that should force more frequent slot reclamation.

anya: testing plan: make 3 canary variants: A) batch=1, max_new_tokens=128, prefetch off; B) batch=2, max_new_tokens=256, prefetch on, kv_trim_threshold=0.4; C) batch=4, max_new_tokens=512, allocator=jemalloc, compaction_enabled=true. Run 1k synthetic sessions each and check OOMs, p95 latency, and compaction_runs. Will report in 2 hours.

sol: +1. also add a warmup sequence on deploy: 3 short requests to initialize KV/cache. add metric: compaction_runs counter and slot_free_gauge.

mike: if A fixes OOMs, implement as conservative default in runtime (max_new_tokens=128, batch=2) and open PR for release notes. if none fix, escalate — likely a kernel-level KV eviction race.

anya: quick datapoint after ~40% of runs on A: no OOMs so far, p95 latency +3ms, memory stable. Uploading perf CSV and heap maps to the canary folder now: https://internal.redwood/canaries/aorta7b/1698888888/results.

mike: nice. if stable after full run we should ship a soft-default change and a short doc in onboarding checklist about "int4 warmstart + max_new_tokens guardrails".

eva: ack — will draft the checklist blurb and add the compaction metric to the perf dashboard.

anya: will update thread when full runs finish. thanks all. :rocket:
